summary.one_liner: PyGObject is a Python package that provides bindings for GObject-based libraries such as GTK, GStreamer, WebKitGTK, GLib and GIO.
summary.what_it_does: PyGObject exposes GLib, GObject, GIO, GTK and other GObject-based libraries to Python code. The README names GTK, GStreamer, WebKitGTK, GLib and GIO as examples and says there are many more. It says it supports Linux, Windows and macOS and works with Python 3.9+ and PyPy3. It is distributed on PyPI as a source distribution that is compiled during installation. The README points to external documentation for OS-specific installation and development setup. It also notes that the default development branch was renamed from master to main and gives git commands for updating a local checkout.
use_cases: build a GTK desktop application in Python
use GStreamer multimedia pipelines from Python
control WebKitGTK web views from Python
access GLib or GIO APIs from Python scripts
notable: Brings GTK, GStreamer, WebKitGTK, GLib and GIO into Python through GObject introspection-style bindings
Works with PyPy3 as well as CPython
caveats: Distributed only as a source distribution, so a C compiler is required on the host
OS-specific setup is delegated to external Getting Started documentation
